name: Brijwasi Sweets, Original Since 1946 - GD Group - Nana Chowk
description:
In the early forties, a young man from Braj in Mathura, landed on the shores of the bustling metropolis called Mumbai. He arrived with a dream to have his own shop selling traditional mithais from his beloved Braj Bhoomi. While he established his first outlet in Kalbadevi, little did he know that he was in fact pioneering a leading chain of stores which would one day become a household name! This was our patriarch Ramswarup ji...

Subsequently, his son Bankelalji, and his succeeding present generations, have grown from strength to strength from that first outlet to several others across the city today. We continue to follow the age old traditional recipes to bring you the finest flavours in our products.

featured_reviews.name: Kaushal Sompura
featured_reviews.review_text:
As one enters the shop everything looks very clean and organised. The staff is well trained in informing about their history, exchanging pleasantries and manages to put up a smile but what actually matters is their Mithais that they are selling which are not fresh!!!

This was the first time I bought an Ice Halwa, varieties of Pedas (white & brown) and some khakharas. They don't provide any sample tasting of their Mithais. Later upon the manager's intervention I was given a small sample of their brown peda which was fresh but not the other white peda or the Ice Halwa... I found that odd but went ahead on the trust of their rich legacy which was told to me by their staff... This was the first red flag.

Even though the staff knew that the sweets have gone stale they still sold it to me.  Upon tasting, I found out the truth about their stale mithai and also found out that they had not provided me with an invoice :-( Second red flag.

Now as I join the dots and it all makes sense that they probably have got good at clearing their stale products off the shelf and making money...
This was not experience that I had hoped for...

featured_reviews.name: ZARIF AHMAD
featured_reviews.review_text: Tried some amazing desserts at Tawakkal Sweets and every bite was absolutely worth it.The Tawakkal Special Dry Fruit Malpua was rich, soft and loaded with dry fruits, perfectly soaked in sweetness. The Fresh Malai was creamy and fresh, while the Matka Rabdi had that authentic thick texture and traditional flavour.Their Classic White Rose Firni was light with a beautiful hint of rose, the Kesar Firni had a lovely saffron aroma, and the Royale Mango Firni was a refreshing twist with delicious mango flavour. If you love traditional mithai and creamy desserts, this place is definitely a must-try.

featured_reviews.name: DV
featured_reviews.review_text: This is Bori or Bora Mohalla located in South Mumbai in between Grant road and Charni road;near about Bhendi Bazaar. It is bustling with non vegetarian fast food served by many famous and age old jaunts like Tawakkal, Surti Handi, Haji tikka and many such. You can get a hot, frsh chicken tikka roll for as less as 90/- Rupees, Baida Roti for 100/- Rs. and Kababs for 140/- Rs. The dishes here are authentic Mughlai and hugely recommended. There is a variety of Muslim sweets available at Tawaqqal and some other outlets too. Some jaunts offer seating as well for couples and families. It is a feast to savour at these outlets during Ramzan.

featured_reviews.name: SANIYA Haji
featured_reviews.review_text:
Here’s what we tried 👇
Ramzan special menu .Must Try at Tawakkal sweets

🥩 Mutton Seekh Burrah – Juicy, smoky and perfectly spiced. The char on the outside with tender meat inside? Absolute win.

🍲 Nalli Nihari – Rich, slow-cooked gravy with melt-in-the-mouth nalli. Deep flavours, comforting and full of warmth.

🍚 Malai Seekh Biryani – Creamy, mildly spiced and loaded with flavour. The malai seekh added a unique twist to classic biryani.

🌯 Butter Chicken Roll – Soft, flavour-packed and indulgent. Perfect grab-and-go option.

🥚 Baida Roti – Crispy outside, stuffed and satisfying. A proper Bohri Mohalla classic.

🍯 Malpua – Sweet, soft and soaked just right — the perfect ending to a hearty meal

featured_reviews.review_text: I went here with my friends for Ramadan food walk. This place had created an outside seating arrangement for food. They had verity of food dishes. They were good but it could have been better. Also one thing stand out was they had female who were taking food orders which was also really great practice. featured_reviews.name: shagir gauri
featured_reviews.review_text: Superb place. I am not a foodie guy and don't understand much about taste. But for first time I would say this place has some great taste and good service. I would give it a double 5star

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Crowded as expected with good food. If you find an empty table run for it.
The chicken and mutton baida roti were delicious but the mutton was significantly better.
The bheja tawa fry was rich and tasty, perfect with lemon. Didn't disappoint. Their rumali roti is soft and perfect btw.
The gurda(kidney) tasted sort of like liver so it wasn't my thing.
Gravy for the nalli was decent but the nalli itself was impossible to break, very disappointing. They didn't help us break it either. I'd say for 700rs it's the most disappointing thing on the menu.
Seekh kebabs were surprisingly fresh and savoury.
Overall a decent place, they just need to work on the quantity of their food and the way they serve nalli.

featured_reviews.name: Kuldip Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shabbir Tawakkal Sweets, Bohri Mohalla ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
No food crawl through Bohri Mohalla is complete without a stop at Shabbir Tawakkal. This legendary sweet shop has been satisfying Mumbai’s sweet tooth for decades and remains an absolute staple of the neighbourhood.
The Mawa Samosa and Malpua are must-orders — rich, indulgent, and made with an expertise that only comes from years of doing one thing really well. Every bite feels homemade in the best possible way.
But come Ramadan, Shabbir Tawakkal transforms into something truly special. The dinner spread is legendary — the Nalli Nihari is fall-off-the-bone perfection, slow-cooked to a depth of flavour that’s almost impossible to describe, and the Bheja Fry is simply to die for. Rich, spiced, and utterly satisfying after a long day of fasting. The atmosphere during Ramadan nights in Bohri Mohalla is electric, and this place sits right at the heart of it.
The shop is small, always busy, and completely unpretentious. No fancy packaging, no gimmicks — just exceptional food that keeps people coming back generation after generation.
Visit any time of year, but if you can make it during Ramadan — absolutely do not miss it.

featured_reviews.name: Ken George
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Shabbir’s Tawakkal Sweets in March and honestly, what an experience.

The variety itself is crazy… so many options to choose from, and everything just looked too good. And the taste? Easily some of the best I’ve had. Every single thing we tried was just amazing.

From the kebabs to the rolls to the naan sandwich, everything was packed with flavour. You can actually tell they know what they’re doing when it comes to food.

And then the desserts… just next level. By that point I was already full but still couldn’t resist trying more.

In fact, it was so good that I had to go back again within 2 days, this time with a bigger group just so I could try more items 😄

Honestly, I just wish I had more space in my stomach that day to eat more. Definitely a place I’ll keep going back to.

featured_reviews.name: Dhanraj Pandit
featured_reviews.review_text: Went during Ramadan but forgot to post this review. Staff and owner are very welcoming. We tried the Tandoori leg piece, mutton seekh, firni (didn't take a photo), and the kunafa was very tasty. Must try if you visit nearby.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Shabbir's Tawakkal Sweets in Bohri Mohalla after hearing a lot about their famous snacks and rolls. The place had a very authentic old Mumbai street food vibe with huge crowds and quick service. We tried the Chicken Kathi Roll and the Mutton Bhuna Naan Sandwich during our visit.

The Chicken Kathi Roll was really good with juicy filling, balanced spices and proper street style flavour. The Mutton Bhuna Naan Sandwich, however, felt average compared to the hype surrounding this place. Overall, it is a good spot to experience Bohri Mohalla food culture and popular Mumbai street food.

featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Badri
featured_reviews.review_text:
My photos don't justify how amazing and good this spot is. The heartbeat of the bhendi Bazar food scene. Family owned ; has their own unique selling items and have maintained the quality of food and sweet served.
Their malpua Rabdi, mango malaai are to die for. The grills and seekhs are part of the menu but their sweet dish options are not to be missed.

featured_reviews.name: ibrahim attari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tawakkal Sweets is one of the best sweet shops for delicious and fresh sweets. The quality of the sweets is excellent, and every item tastes rich, authentic, and perfectly made. The shop maintains good hygiene and cleanliness, which makes the overall experience even better. The staff is very polite, friendly, and quick in service, helping customers with a positive attitude.
I especially loved the freshness and flavor of their sweets and snacks. Everything feels freshly prepared with good ingredients and balanced sweetness. The atmosphere of the shop is nice and welcoming, making it a great place to visit with family and friends. Whether you want sweets for festivals, special occasions, or regular cravings, this place is a perfect choice. Highly recommended for anyone looking for quality sweets, good service, and a satisfying experience.

Its very sweet, testy and delicious.

Indian desserts are not just limited to a post-meal treat as one can have them whenever they crave the taste (in limited amounts for health reasons) and relish its taste. From fruits and vegetables to several other raw products you can easily source from your kitchen, there’s something sweet for everyone.

Here are some interesting facts (recipes included) about some of the most delicious desserts you can relish on special days with your friends and family members or even when you want to treat yourself on a cheat day.

Motichoor Laddoos: With a base of chickpea flour, these deep-fried saffron colour balls resemble doughnuts. Their rich taste comprises the smoothness of pure ghee. The sweet dish, which has its origins in North India, is often seasoned with saffron or melon seeds and sweetened with thickened sugar syrup. The balls are also occasionally mixed with orange food colouring, to make their hue truly pop.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Daryush Bakery founded in 1929 is a popular bakery since ages. It’s a 5 min walk from Charni Road Station.
Daryush Bakery is small, compact like most bakeries & offers bread, dry snacks, puffs, pastries, cupcakes & cakes.

Decor & Ambience is minimal & it hardly has seating capacity of 4-6 people.

Note :- Daryush is 100% Vegetarian.
They also do Vegan & Gluten free cakes (0.5 kg & 1 kg cakes on customised order).

To try a bit of everything I ordered the following items :-
1. Chocolate Truffle Cupcake - Rs 25/-
2. Mawa Cake - Decent taste but a bit dry for my liking.
3. Chocolate chip cookies - 2 cookies per pack & it cost Rs 30 /-
4. Maska Khaari - 200gm for Rs 70/-
5. Veg Puff - Rs 20/-
6. Paneer Puff - Rs 30/-

I think from my entire order other than the mawa cake which was ok, everything else was great @ Daryush Bakery.

Pros :-
1. Daryush started in 1929 & is still going strong. Kudos to the longevity shown by them.
2. Daryush offers a wide variety of stuff (breads, puffs, cupcakes, pastries & cakes) for a customer to choose from.
3. Daryush offers Good quality, decent quantity & excellent pricing.

Cons
1. Bakery is small, compact with minimal decor. ( Could definitely improve )
2. They don’t offer much seating. Max 4-6 ppl can sit at the max.
3. Cake variety can definitely increase.
4. Takeaway Bag should be given along with takeaway boxes. Please Note.

Overall I had a satisfying experience @ Daryush Bakery & frankly it doesn’t surprise me why they have stayed open for so long. Keep it up guys 👍

featured_reviews.name: Mithil Thakker
featured_reviews.review_text:
Daryush Bakery is one of the oldest gem hidden in the streets of Girgaon area in South Mumbai .
.
.
They are known for serving some amazing edible products right from pastries to Cookies to Biscuits and many more since pre-independence era of  1929
.
.
Our all time favourite snack from here is
Veg Panneer Puff which is a simple but extremely Delicious delight from this bakery served along with tangy ketchup .
.
.
Besides this they have one of the best Shrewsbury Biscuits in town & also not to forget the amazing chocolate walnut fudge which is a bit on a bitter side for all those dark chocolate lovers .
.
.
You may also indulge in their sweet Chocolate Cookies & ultra soft Chocolate Brownie to satisfy your crave for  chocolate
.
.
Pastry is one aspect where they need a slight improvement . We tried their Red Velvet Pastry which was the last price left for the day . The upper Creamy part was just too good however the lower part had got a bit dry may be as it was kept in refrigerator since afternoon .
.
.
Overall a Sweet Experience at one of our most favourite bakery in town .
.
.
Thank You for reading my detailed Review .
.
.

featured_reviews.name: Freya Gabani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Daryush Bakery founded in 1929 is a popular bakery since ages. It’s a 5 min walk from Charni Road Station.
Daryush Bakery is small, compact like most bakeries & offers bread, dry snacks, puffs, pastries, cupcakes & cakes.

Decor & Ambience is minimal & it hardly has seating capacity of 4-6 people.

Note :- Daryush is 100% Vegetarian.
They also do Vegan & Gluten free cakes (0.5 kg & 1 kg cakes on customised order).

Pros :-
1. Daryush started in 1929 & is still going strong. Kudos to the longevity shown by them.
2. Daryush offers a wide variety of stuff (breads, puffs, cupcakes, pastries & cakes) for a customer to choose from.
3. Daryush offers Good quality, decent quantity & excellent pricing.

Cons
1. Bakery is small, compact with minimal decor. ( Could definitely improve )
2. They don’t offer much seating. Max 4-6 ppl can sit at the max.
3. Cake variety can definitely increase.
4. Takeaway Bag should be given along with takeaway boxes. Please Note.

Overall I had a satisfying experience @ Daryush Bakery & frankly it doesn’t surprise me why they have stayed open for so long. Keep it up guys 👍
